source.title: The Geometry of Neural Nets' Parameter Spaces Under Reparametrization
source.authors: Agustinus Kristiadi; Felix Dangel; Philipp Hennig

page_placements.theme: Curvature and flatness are conditional generalization correlates

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; some equations and tables appear flattened or corrupted in transcription, but the relevant numerical results are legible.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own comparisons showing that Hessian sharpness can change under reparametrization without changing generalization, challenging sharpness as a generalization measure unless made invariant. This refines V7's sharpness–gap relation.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR-10 optimizer and reparametrization results measure sharpness and generalization gap and bear on V7. The MNIST, FMNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 test accuracies compare optimizers but do not by themselves test V4's held-out performance claim; they are omitted. Other generalization claims in the introduction and references are cited or discussed, not tested here.
record.test_reason: Table 2 tests V4 in additional image-classification settings: Adam has lower test accuracy than momentum SGD on four datasets under a fixed, minimally tuned recipe. The ordinary Hessian-trace experiments do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate for the sharpness discussion but narrower than the overall conclusion. The authors argue that explicitly tracking the metric and applying the appropriate geometric transformation rules preserves reparametrization invariance for Hessian-derived quantities, optimization dynamics, and density modes. They do not establish that an invariant sharpness measure predicts generalization better.
record.recipe_differences: The paper studies reparametrization invariance of geometric quantities, including Hessian-based sharpness; its CIFAR-10 experiment uses ordinary Hessian trace and parameter scaling rather than the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.method_sensitivity: Reparametrizing SGD by scaling parameters changes Hessian-trace sharpness while the reported generalization gap stays the same.

fits_no_version.finding: SGD's CIFAR-10 generalization gap remains 5.2% while ordinary Hessian trace changes from 1531.8 to 6143.7 or 383.6 under coordinate scaling; default Adam has gap 7.2% and trace 1929.8.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Ordinary Hessian-trace sharpness can change under function-preserving reparametrization without changing generalization, making its cross-model ordering coordinate dependent.

record.problems: The generalization evidence relevant to V7 is one CIFAR-10 model family and a small set of reparametrizations. The authors' experiment does not test the magnitude-aware measure named in V7; the reparametrization results concern ordinary Hessian trace.
record.rows_left_out: The paper reports separate optimizer test accuracies in Appendix E.2, Table 2 for MNIST, FMNIST, CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100. These compare held-out accuracy, but do not test V4's specified limited-tuning comparison, so they were not extracted as claim-version rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its comparison with natural-label generalization.
Test error across widths beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Learning-rate search fairness, broader tuning, language benchmarks, decoupled weight decay, and switching optimizers. The study uses chosen defaults rather than reporting a tuning sweep.
Batch-size comparisons and adaptations to large-batch training.
Dropout and its interactions with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.

The magnitude-aware perturbation measure, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Ordinary Hessian-trace non-invariance does not establish failure of this measure.
Removing memorized versus random training examples.

missing.what: Add the SGD–Adam held-out accuracy comparisons for all four datasets. Although rows_left_out declares Table 2, its exclusion as irrelevant to V4 is mistaken; these results test the limited-recipe comparison and supply the verdict's evidence.

record.verdict_notes: Remove both extracted V7 verdicts. Neither ordinary Hessian-trace non-invariance nor its default-parametrization association tests the magnitude-aware measure specified in V7. V4 support is descriptive and confined to the reported fixed recipes.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and natural-label generalization.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image generalization.
Adaptive versus SGD held-out performance under the version's tuning conditions.
Large-batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.

The paper does not compare magnitude-aware sharpness against norm- or margin-based measures, nor test the stated CIFAR-10 and SVHN convolutional-family setup without augmentation. Its results concern ordinary Hessian trace under reparametrization on CIFAR-10.

relationships.condition: LeNet on MNIST and FMNIST; WiderResNet-16-4 on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; default Adam versus SGD with Nesterov momentum; 100 epochs with cosine annealing.
relationships.reason: Table 2 reports SGD/Adam test accuracies of 99.3/99.2, 92.9/92.6, 94.9/92.4, and 76.8/71.9%, respectively, averaged over five seeds. Based on text because these results were omitted from the rows; uncertainty and tuning sweeps are not reported.
relationships.display_finding: Reported test accuracies favor SGD with Nesterov momentum over Adam across all four benchmarks, but these comparisons remain unverified and lack reported uncertainty.
